Russia.text: Three-fourths of its people live in urban areas.
Russia.evidence: It is a highly urbanised country, with three-fourths of its population living in urban areas.

Turkey.text: Only a smaller part, East Thrace, is in Europe; most of the country lies in Anatolia in West Asia.
Turkey.evidence: Turkey, officially the Republic of Türkiye, is a country mainly located in Anatolia in West Asia, with a smaller part called East Thrace in Southeast Europe.

Germany.text: Berlin is its most populous city, but its largest urban area is the Ruhr.
Germany.evidence: The nation's capital and most populous city is Berlin and its main financial centre is Frankfurt; the largest urban area is the Ruhr.

United Kingdom.text: At its 1920s height, its empire covered around a quarter of the world's landmass and population.
United Kingdom.evidence: At its height in the 1920s, the empire encompassed around a quarter of the world's landmass and population, and was the largest in history.

France.text: Five of its 18 regions are overseas, among them French Guiana in South America.
France.evidence: Its overseas regions and territories include French Guiana in South America, ... Its 18 integral regions—five of which are overseas—span a combined area of 632,702 km2 (244,288 sq mi),

Italy.text: Besides the peninsula, it takes in nearly 800 islands, notably Sicily and Sardinia.
Italy.evidence: It consists of a peninsula, which extends into the Mediterranean Sea, with the Alps on its northern land border, as well as nearly 800 islands, notably Sicily and Sardinia.

Spain.text: Its territory includes Ceuta and Melilla, two autonomous cities in mainland Africa.
Spain.evidence: its territory also includes the Canary Islands, in the Eastern Atlantic Ocean; the Balearic Islands, in the Western Mediterranean Sea; and the autonomous cities of Ceuta and Melilla, in mainland Africa.

Ukraine.text: Humans have inhabited it since at least 32,000 BC.
Ukraine.evidence: Humans have inhabited Ukraine since at least 32,000 BC.

Poland.text: Its Commonwealth with Lithuania adopted Europe's first modern constitution in 1791.
Poland.evidence: The Kingdom of Poland emerged in 1025, and in 1569 cemented its long-standing association with Lithuania, thus forming the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth. At the time, the Commonwealth was one of the great powers of Europe, with an elective monarchy and a uniquely liberal political system, which adopted Europe's first modern constitution in 1791.

Kazakhstan.text: With fewer than 8 people per square kilometre, it has one of the lowest population densities in the world.
Kazakhstan.evidence: Kazakhstan has a population of 20.6 million and one of the lowest population densities in the world, with fewer than 8 people per square kilometre (21 people/mi2).
